## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Artifact Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_metadata_store" "store" {
  name        = "store"
  description = "Store to test Artifact"
  region      = "us-central1"
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_artifact" "artifact" {
  artifact_id    = "artifact"
  metadatastore  = google_vertex_ai_metadata_store.store.name
  location       = "us-central1"
  schema_title   = "system.Dataset"
  schema_version = "0.0.1"
  uri            = "https://example.com/dataset"
  state          = "PENDING"
  
  metadata = {
    key = "value"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the Artifact.

* `metadatastore` -
  (Required)
  The metadata store of the Artifact.

* `artifact_id` -
  (Required)
  The {artifact} portion of the resource name with the format:
  `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/metadataStores/{metadatastore}/artifacts/{artifact}`.
  If not provided, the Artifact's ID will be a UUID generated by the service.
  Must be 4-128 characters in length. Valid characters are `/a-z-/`.
  Must be unique across all Artifacts in the parent MetadataStore.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Description of the Artifact

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User provided display name of the Artifact.
  May be up to 128 Unicode characters.

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The labels with user-defined metadata to organize your Artifacts.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Properties of the Artifact.

* `schema_title` -
  (Optional)
  The title of the schema describing the metadata.

* `schema_version` -
  (Optional)
  The version of the schema in schema_name to use.

* `state` -
  (Optional)
  The state of this Artifact. This is a property of the Artifact, and does
  not imply or capture any ongoing process. This property is managed by
  clients (such as Vertex AI Pipelines), and the system does not prescribe
  or check the validity of state transitions.
  Possible values are: `PENDING`, `LIVE`.

* `uri` -
  (Optional)
  The uniform resource identifier of the artifact file.
  May be empty if there is no actual artifact file.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/metadataStores/{{metadatastore}}/artifacts/{{artifact_id}}`

* `create_time` -
  Timestamp when this Artifact was created.

* `name` -
  The resource name of the Artifact.

* `update_time` -
  Timestamp when this Artifact was last updated.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


Artifact can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/metadataStores/{{metadatastore}}/artifacts/{{artifact_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{metadatastore}}/{{artifact_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{metadatastore}}/{{artifact_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import Artifact using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    metadatastore = "<-required value->"
    artifactId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_artifact.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import Artifact using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/metadataStores/{{metadatastore}}/artifacts/{{artifact_id}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_artifact.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), Artifact can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_artifact.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/metadataStores/{{metadatastore}}/artifacts/{{artifact_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_artifact.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{metadatastore}}/{{artifact_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_artifact.default {{location}}/{{metadatastore}}/{{artifact_id}}
```
